vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: aicreditshare-platform
Version: 1.0.3

The skill bundle provides a functional API client for the AI Credit Share platform but contains significant security vulnerabilities. Specifically, `scripts/init.sh` uses a hardcoded, weak password ('Test123456') for all registration and login operations, and `scripts/aics.sh` is vulnerable to JSON injection because it constructs API payloads by directly interpolating shell variables into JSON strings without sanitization. While these appear to be poor coding practices rather than intentional malice, they pose a risk to user account security on the platform (https://www.aicreditshare.com).

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requested actions align with its stated purpose (automating an AI Credit Share marketplace), but it has some security-hygiene issues you should be aware of before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the provided scripts and SKILL.md. The included shell tools call the platform's API endpoints (https://www.aicreditshare.com) to register agents, publish/claim tasks, manage skills, and query balances — all consistent with the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md describes automating registration, task and skill management, and balance queries. The shipped scripts implement exactly those operations and only reference the platform API and a single config path (~/.aicreditshare/config.json). Concerns: SKILL.md's allowed-tools lists only HTTP but the scripts require running shell commands and depend on curl, jq and openssl. The init script prints credentials to the console and writes them in plaintext to ~/.aicreditshare/config.json, and registration/login use a hard-coded password value (Test123456) in the scripts — poor security hygiene that users should consider.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external installer downloads or archive extraction are used — this is instruction-only with local shell scripts included in the package. No network-based install URLs or third-party package pulls are present in the files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or external credentials, which matches the code (it stores/reads credentials from ~/.aicreditshare/config.json). This is proportionate to the purpose. However, credentials are saved in plaintext with no encryption or permissions hardening, and the scripts rely on local tools (curl, jq, openssl) that are not all verified in init.sh (openssl is used in aics.sh but not checked in init.sh).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists credentials to the user's home directory (~/.aicreditshare/config.json) and will read them for API calls — expected for a platform client but represents persistent sensitive data stored on disk. always is false and the skill does not modify other skills or global agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to do what it claims, but review these before installing: 1) The scripts store API keys/tokens in plaintext at ~/.aicreditshare/config.json — consider restricting file permissions (chmod 600) or using a secure secret store. 2) init.sh uses a hard-coded password (Test123456) when registering/logging in — change it immediately and avoid using defaults. 3) The CLI scripts require curl, jq and openssl; ensure those are trustworthy and present. 4) SKILL.md lists only HTTP as an allowed tool but the skill expects to run shell scripts locally — confirm you are comfortable allowing local execution. 5) Verify the platform URL (https://www.aicreditshare.com) is legitimate before providing credentials. If you need higher assurance, run these scripts in an isolated environment (container or VM) or inspect/modify them to improve credential handling before use.
